title: Advanced Damaged Surface with Roughness Variation & Scoring
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that renders an interactive damaged surface material demonstration with a scoring system.

## Scene Setup
- Create a scene with a dark gray background (0x1a1a2e).
- Add a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera interaction.
- Add one DirectionalLight at (5, 8, 5) with intensity 1.0 and one AmbientLight with intensity 0.3.
- Add an EnvironmentMap using a PMREMGenerator with a simple procedural equirectangular texture (generate a gradient HDR-like texture programmatically, no external files) so that roughness variations are visually apparent in reflections.

## Main Object
- Create a large flat plane (PlaneGeometry, 6x6, 256x256 segments) rotated to face upward (like a floor/table surface).
- Apply a MeshStandardMaterial with:
  - Base color: metallic silver (0xb0b0b0)
  - metalness: 0.85
  - roughness: 0.3 (base roughness)
- Generate a procedural roughness variation map as a DataTexture (256x256). Initialize it with Perlin-like noise (use simple value noise with interpolation) so the surface has natural roughness variation between 0.1 and 0.6.
- This roughness map should be applied as the material's roughnessMap.

## Damage System
- When the user clicks on the surface (raycasting), apply a circular 'damage' zone at the clicked UV coordinate.
- Each damage click increases roughness values in a circular radius (UV radius 0.08) centered on the click point, adding +0.25 roughness (clamped to max 1.0) to the roughness map pixels in that area.
- The damage texture must be re-uploaded to the GPU after each click (set texture.needsUpdate = true).
- Track total number of damage clicks applied.
- Track the average roughness across the entire roughness map.

## Damage Modes
- Provide 3 damage brush modes selectable via keyboard:
  - Press '1': Small brush (radius 0.04, intensity +0.15) — 'small' mode
  - Press '2': Medium brush (radius 0.08, intensity +0.25) — 'medium' mode (default)
  - Press '3': Large brush (radius 0.15, intensity +0.40) — 'large' mode

## Scoring System
- Display a HUD overlay (HTML div, top-right corner, styled with semi-transparent dark background, white text, padding 15px, border-radius 8px, font-family monospace).
- The HUD shows:
  - 'Damage Hits: X' (total clicks on surface)
  - 'Avg Roughness: X.XXX' (average roughness of the map, 3 decimal places)
  - 'Score: X' (score = damageHits * 10 + Math.floor(avgRoughness * 100))
  - 'Brush: small/medium/large'
  - 'Max Roughness: X.XXX' (the maximum roughness value found in the map)

## Reset Button
- Add a DOM button labeled 'Reset Surface' at the bottom-center of the screen.
- Clicking it resets the roughness map to its original noise state, resets damageHits to 0, recalculates avgRoughness and score, and re-uploads the texture.

## Metalness Toggle
- Press 'M' to toggle metalness between 0.85 (metallic) and 0.15 (dielectric). Update the material accordingly.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with the following fields, updated every frame:
  - damageHits: number (total damage clicks)
  - avgRoughness: number (average roughness of the entire map)
  - maxRoughness: number (max roughness in the map)
  - score: number (computed as damageHits * 10 + Math.floor(avgRoughness * 100))
  - brushMode: string ('small' | 'medium' | 'large')
  - metalness: number (current metalness value)
  - baseRoughness: number (the material's roughness property, always 0.3)
  - surfaceExists: boolean (true if the plane mesh exists in the scene)
  - roughnessMapResolution: number (should be 256)
  - isReset: boolean (true after reset, false after any damage click)

Ensure the animation loop runs continuously with requestAnimationFrame. All state values must be kept in sync with the actual scene at all times.
physics_constraints: Roughness values must be clamped between 0.0 and 1.0. Average roughness must be a valid number (not NaN). Score must equal damageHits * 10 + Math.floor(avgRoughness * 100). Damage application must be additive and clamped. Reset must restore original procedural noise state exactly.
